about: We're a hands-on club for kids. Members learn by doing: building things, getting outdoors, helping the community, and trying something new every month.
Families are part of the fun. Parents and guardians help run activities, and every adult volunteer is screened and trained before working with kids.

pillars.title: Try New Things
pillars.text: A new skill or adventure every month, from knots to robots.

pillars.title: Get Outside
pillars.text: Hikes, park days, and outdoor games in every season.

pillars.title: Help Others
pillars.text: Service projects that make our neighborhood better.

pillars.title: Make Friends
pillars.text: A welcoming group where every kid belongs.

groups.name: Explorers
groups.text: Short, playful activities with a parent or guardian alongside.

groups.name: Trailblazers
groups.text: Bigger projects, outdoor skills, and first chances to lead.

groups.name: Leaders
groups.text: Plan activities, mentor younger members, and take on challenges.

groups_intro: Members meet in small groups by age, and the whole club comes together for big events.

join_steps.title: Say Hello
join_steps.text: Email us with your child's name and age. We'll answer any questions.

join_steps.title: Visit a Meeting
join_steps.text: Come see what we're about. No commitment, no cost.

join_steps.title: Sign Up
join_steps.text: Fill out the registration and permission forms, and you're in.

uniform: No uniform needed. Wear clothes that can get a little messy. Some clubs use a club T-shirt; ask us.

safety.title: Keeping Kids Safe
points: Two trained, background-checked adults are present at every activity. No adult is ever alone with a child who isn't their own.
Parents and guardians are always welcome at meetings.
We post photos of members only with written permission from a parent or guardian, and never with a child's full name.

faq.q: When and where do you meet?
Can we visit before we join?
faq.a: Yes! Come to any meeting. Email {email} first so we can watch for you.
Parents and guardians are always welcome, and younger members need an adult with them. We also need volunteers; no experience needed.

faq.q: How do you keep kids safe?
faq.a: Every adult volunteer is screened and trained, and two adults are present at every activity. See our Privacy & Safety page for our photo rules.
